newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices mixed in pre-holiday lull.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices mixed in pre-holiday lull.

text.p: Danish bond prices opened mixed on Wednesday, expected to be a quiet day ahead of Thursday's Constitution Day market holiday.
"There is the prospect of further price rises, even though Danish investors might be a little reticent on Wednesday due to Thursday's holdiday," a dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 opened at 111.14, yielding 6.30 percent, unchanged from Tuesday's close.
The seven percent 2007 bond traded at 103.87, yielding 6.47 percent, up from around 103.57 at close of business on Tuesday.
The crown firmed to 3.8080 to the mark from 3.8085.
The 2006 benchmark's yield gap with Germany was 45 basis points, compared to Tuesday's 46 bp and the 2007 gap to the bund also one basis point narrower, at 65 bp.
The 2006 bond's June future, expiring on June 16, was up 0.18 point to 111.08.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 was up 0.07 point to 89.25. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969650
